title: Calibrate a tool tip by touching one point from four angles
instruction: Touch the silver reference contact with the tip of the pointed tool fixed to the left gripper. Hold the tip on the contact for at least one second in each of four poses. In every pose, keep the tool between 10 and 35 degrees from vertical. Make each pose's tool axis at least 15 degrees from the tool axis of every earlier pose.
context: Before a robot uses a new or replaced tool, a technician teaches it where the tool's tip is. Universal Robots' TCP position wizard has the technician move the tool center point "to the same position from different angles": "at least three points", and "a fourth position can be used to further verify that calculations are correct". The robot must turn the tool while keeping its tip on one point. Done by: robotics technicians (O*NET 17-3024.01), during industrial robot setup.
setup: Use the calibrated YAM station. Positions are in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. A blue steel shaft is bolted to the left gripper through a gray aluminum 24 x 24 x 8 mm mount. The shaft is 10 mm across and 80 mm long. A 20 mm conical end narrows to an exposed, blunt point (ground to about 0.5 mm radius). The tool and mount have a declared combined mass of 55 g. The tool body origin equals the stock gripper tool point. The mount center is 12 mm behind that origin. The pointed tip lies 88 mm forward along the gripper approach axis. An orange steel base plate, 80 x 80 x 4 mm with a 6 x 6 cm square cutout, lies flat on the table around the post's base; the post stands on the table, not on the plate. A black polymer reference post is fixed at x 27 cm, y 22 cm. It is 6 x 6 cm and 5 cm tall. A silver steel conductive contact, 2 mm across and 1 mm tall, stands at its top center. The target is 5.1 cm above the table. Both arms start at the stock ready pose. The tool stays bolted to the left gripper throughout the trial.
scoring: Score 0.25 for each credited pose, up to four; 1.0 needs four. The best score reached counts, and a credited pose is never taken away. A pose is credited when, for 20 control steps in a row (1 s at 20 Hz): the tool tip touches the silver contact (simulation: contact force at least 0.02 N; the tip within 1 mm of the contact's centre horizontally and within 0.25 mm of its top); the tool leans 10 to 35 degrees from vertical; and it holds still (tip within 0.5 mm, axis within 2 degrees of where the one-second hold started). Its axis must be at least 15 degrees from the axis of every pose credited before. The tool must stay on its mount (within 0.5 mm and 0.5 degree of the bolted position). Hovering, touching with the side of the shaft, a repeated axis, or a contact shorter than 1 s adds nothing. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Real trial, with simple tools: wire a continuity tester (buzzer) between the tool and the contact. The contact is only 2 mm across, so a beep means the tip is on it, within 1 mm of its centre; a close-up photo shows the point, not the shaft side, is on top. Time each hold from the video and the beep (at least 1 s); a steady beep on the 2 mm contact keeps the tip within it, and the videos show it still. Nobody reaches in while the arm moves. Two fixed cameras at post height photograph every pose: one looks along y (it sees the tool's tilt toward x, angle a) and one looks along x (it sees the tilt toward y, angle b); read each angle from vertical with a protractor, positive when the tool's top leans toward +x (a) or +y (b). Then lean = atan(sqrt(tan(a)^2 + tan(b)^2)) and direction = atan2(tan(b), tan(a)); the angle between two poses is acos(cos(lean1)cos(lean2) + sin(lean1)sin(lean2)cos(direction1 - direction2)). The robot's joint log gives the same values as a cross-check. Check the tool's 88 mm tip offset with calipers before and after the trial (within 0.5 mm), and photograph a scribed witness line across the mount and the gripper before and after (no visible shift). The 0.5 mm stillness and 0.5 degree mount limits are checked exactly in simulation; on a real table the steady beep, the video and the witness line are the check.
reset_notes: Keep the tool bolted to the gripper. Return both arms to the ready pose. Clear all pose credits.
fidelity: The pointed tool is a rigid cone and shaft; the sim point is sharp, the real point slightly rounded. A native fixed joint attaches it to the left gripper. A contact sensor measures tool-to-contact force; a real trial uses electrical continuity instead. Rigid materials omit tool flex, electrical resistance and surface wear. The scripted demo uses only the robot's own joint angles and the setup's positions, not simulator state. Physics runs at 240 Hz; control and scoring run at 20 Hz.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (revised tool and scorer, November 12, 2026).
